title: Borg suddenly fails to create archive in server machine over ssh, throws OSError: [Errno 5]

## Have you checked borgbackup docs, FAQ, and open GitHub issues?
yes

## Is this a BUG / ISSUE report or a QUESTION?

Issue

## System information. For client/server mode post info for both machines.

#### Your borg version (borg -V).
borg 1.2.0

#### Operating system (distribution) and version.
client: Ubuntu 20.04 
server: Ubuntu 20.04 

#### Full borg commandline that lead to the problem (leave away excludes and passwords)

borg create  --stats --progress --compression auto,zstd,3 ssh://<email-scrubbed>:xx/myrepo/:<nick> myfiles

## Describe the problem you're observing.
When creating an archive, borg seems to be  `syncing chunks cache` for up to 80%, and then suddenly stops and throws the following error: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):<nick> archive xxxxx

  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/borg/remote.py", line 247, in serve
    res = f(**args)

  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/borg/repository.py", line 1117, in get
    return self.io.read(segment, offset, id)

  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/borg/repository.py", line 1481, in read
    header = fd.read(self.put_header_fmt.size)

OSError: [Errno 5] Input/output error
```
I can however  access the archive over ssh and even list the archives with borg remotely `borg list ssh://<email-scrubbed>:xx/myrepo`, so there is no Input/output issues. Even more, If I can log into server that host the repo, I can create a local archive to the repo without issues.

any way to begin troubleshooting this?  Some of the post suggest clearing cache... how can I do that in the client machine?

Looking at the cache, I see that within the repo ID, there is `/chunks.archive.d` and also `/txn.active`. I don't think I have seen that last file before.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
So, better check that hardware, filesystem, RAM and **only after fixing that** try `borg check`.

If you want a thorough check (that reads all content data), you'll need `borg check --verify-data`.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Creating a new archive does not read content data that is already contained in the repo.

So if there is e.g. some bad sector in some segment file, that will not be discovered.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Wouldn't that be the same when creating a new archive from the client? You don't think this is a cache issue at all? It is just it stops when it is `syncing chunks cache` ...

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
If you use a `ssh://...` repo with borg, the `repository.py` code is executed on the repo server side.

In the traceback you have posted, you see it is crashing there because the OS gave an I/O error to borg instead of the data it wanted to read from some repo segment file.

If the chunks index/cache gets out of sync because you use one repo from multiple places, borg will need to resync that. It then reads infos from ALL archives, either from the local chunks.archives.d/  directory or from the remote repo.

BTW, just as a side note: if you access the repo, always use the same user to not mess up permissions for the repo files (e.g. by sometimes using "borg" and other times using "root").

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I see... I just tried creating an archive from another client that also backs-up to the same remote repo and It is throwing the same error. So if all these seems to indicate that there is a bad sector in a segment file.... is there a way I can fix this to continue backing up to my repo? (I don't mind losing the last archives as long as I haven't lost all the archives) Could you point me in the right direction to solve this? thanks!

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
https://github.com/borgbackup/borg/issues/7426#issuecomment-1464157052 that is the recommeded procedure.

if you do not fix the hw / fs issue first, you might make it worse by running `borg check --repair`.

The overall "SMART health status" is known to switch rather late to "FAILING" (suspicion: HDD manufacturers don't like you to return stuff while it is in warranty).

If you like, post the complete output of `smartctl -a /dev/sdd` (note the absence of the partition number) so we can have a look.

Not sure why you are continuing to work with borg on that defective disk after I advised you should copy the repo to a new disk and continue there. You can just try to cp, rsync or use a file manager to transfer the repo directory to a new disk.

If it can not read all the files, then just copy as much as still readable.

After that is finished, run `borg check --repair` on the repo **on the new disk**.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Sorry I didn't understand your prev recommendation. I'll copy as much as i can and do a `borg check --repair` in the new drive. When copying the repo with rsync, do you recommend keeping the hardlinks as in `rsync -aH` ?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
`rsync -avH src/ dst/` is what I usually use. Maybe also `--numeric-ids`, depending on the use case.

IIRC, borg doesn't use hardlinks inside the repo except for secure erasing the old version of the repo config after it has written an updated one. So using `-H` is maybe not really required, but also does no harm.

If your repo had corruption (like unreadable/missing files), you need to first run `borg check --repair` on the repo on the working hdd.

If that doesn't work, I need the traceback from that.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hey @participant2 , thanks a lot for all your help. I think it is almost fixed.  After running  `borg check --repair ` on the repo and on the archives (and waiting patiently for hours), the missing chucks have been replaced with zeros. Looking at the repair logs, I think the issue could have resulted in part from a file that was being accessed while the automatic borg backup was running... which could have caused a hiccup on the HDD (or the HDD is ready for the trash). In any case, After the repairs, all the repo and archive checks are completed and no problems are found!!! (albeit from the missing chunks that are now zeros).

So my last questios: at this point that all the checks are ok, what should be the best sequence of next steps to deal with missing chunks? A --> B--> C?
A) Clear local cache with ` $ borg delete --cache-only $REPO`
B) Delete corrupted repo(s) from oldest to newest  `$ borg delete --force REPO::CORRUPT_ARCHIVE`
C) Create a new archive and hope the missing chucks are recreated with `$ borg create`

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
It's all fixed now, no more empty or missing chunks. After `borg check --repair` , I deleted the corrupted archive and the newer ones after that (I don't know if this was necessary, but it worked in my case).  I have created archives from different client machines and it all has completed successfully. Doing a `borg check` no longer throws any errors. Also FYI, I didn't need to delete any caches.

Thank's for all the help!

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Usually there is no problem with parallel (read) access to files on linux, so I guess your HDD might be defective. And you shouldn't have multiple things writing to your borg repo in parallel (borg uses locks and nothing else than borg should write into there anyway).

 If you post `smartctl -a /dev/sdx` output, we can have a look (if one looks at the detailled stats, it usually becomes rather clear - just ignore that overall health value).
